# chars.v1.js — character card data

Used by the character card (`#/char/<character>`): Hán Việt, parts, origin, and which stroke belongs to which part,
for every course character (the files in `vendor/hanzi/`) and every part they are built from.
Generated by `tools/build_chars.py` (see its header for how to rebuild). Do not edit by hand.

Sources and licences:

- **Make Me a Hanzi** `dictionary.txt` (https://github.com/skishore/makemeahanzi): decomposition, origin type
  (pictophonetic / ideographic / pictographic), meaning part, sound part, origin hint, and the stroke-to-part matches.
  Licensed under the **GNU LGPL 3.0** (it is derived from Unihan and CJKlib). This file is a modified subset
  (only the fields and characters the card shows). Licence texts: `MAKEMEAHANZI-COPYING-LGPL.txt` (which also holds
  the Unicode notice) and `GPL-3.0.txt`, which the LGPL refers to. The data stays under the LGPL; the rest of the app is
  not affected because it only loads this file.
- **hanviet-pinyin-words** 2.1.7 (https://github.com/ph0ngp/hanviet-pinyin-words), © 2024 Phong Phan, **MIT** —
  Hán Việt readings chosen by pinyin. Licence: `HANVIET-MIT-LICENSE.txt`.
- **Unicode Unihan** (via the `cjk-unihan` npm package's SQLite copy): traditional forms (to look up Hán Việt),
  English definitions where Make Me a Hanzi has none, and `kVietnamese` as a last fallback.
  © Unicode, Inc., Unicode licence (notice in `MAKEMEAHANZI-COPYING-LGPL.txt`). The data was modified (subset).
- Radical names and the short Vietnamese meanings of parts (`rn`, `rv`): written for this app.

The app downloads this file the first time a card is opened (about 50 KB compressed) and keeps it offline.
When the content changes, save it under a new name (`chars.v2.js`) and update `CHARS_URL` in `js/app/11-chars.js`.
